A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material and renumbered figures.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-training results, geometry optimizations, molecular-dynamics simulations, and fine-tuning experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds OC20 training and validation results in Appendix G.

M1.justification: Both versions describe joint PET-M training, conservative fine-tuning, and the same multiple-time-stepping procedure. V2 newly explains that the non-conservative head also remains trained during fine-tuning; this disclosure does not establish a change to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds an OC20 S2EF subset to the fine-tuning experiments in Appendix G; v1 discussed OC20 only as prior work. Existing water, QM9, MPtrj, graphene, amorphous-carbon, and aluminium coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding retained experiments. The added OC20 experiment uses the existing comparison between PET-C, PET-NC, and a conservatively fine-tuned model; the changed fine-tuned curve label does not introduce another comparator.

E3.justification: The water learning curves change from validation force RMSE to MAE and place fine-tuning after pretraining on the GPU-time axis. The new OC20 protocol trains on the first 15,000 samples of the 200k S2EF training set and validates on the next 5,000. Retained simulation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G revises the training-efficiency analysis and extends its comparison of fine-tuning versus training from scratch to OC20, with complete learning curves. Existing thermostat sensitivity, optimization-failure, closed-loop-work, and multiple-time-stepping analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Tables 2 and 7 retain their uncertainty reporting, and structural-correlation figures retain bands encompassing two standard errors. No new repeated-run counts, seed information, or statistical testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Appendix G changes the reported time needed to match conservative training accuracy from about one-eighth to one-third of total training time and adds OC20 convergence results. Water curves are replaced under revised metric and time reporting, preventing a direct accuracy comparison across versions. Existing numerical tables and simulation findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 broadens the Jacobian-asymmetry diagnostic by permitting any other matrix norm alongside the Frobenius norm. The displayed formula, other equations, harmonic-mode derivation, computational-cost reasoning, and multiple-time-stepping formulation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims remain that non-conservative forces can compromise optimization and molecular dynamics, while hybrid models can accelerate training and simulations. V2 adds emphasis on future universal interatomic potentials without materially changing these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.7 removes the good-thermostat qualification from its expectation that sufficiently accurate non-conservative models can reach low-energy structures. Section 4.8 also drops the explicit assertion that analogous acceleration can readily extend to geometry optimization. Most mechanism explanations and limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V2 replaces a promised future release with a stated code/data location at Zenodo record 14778891 and discloses continued training of the direct-force head during fine-tuning. Software versions are retained in Appendix I, but v1's explicit nanoPET/metatrain implementation reference is removed.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and substantive positioning relative to conservative models, direct-force prediction, and symmetry learning are retained. OC20's citation already appears in v1; its new experimental use does not add a related work.

P1.justification: V2 copyedits the main text, rewrites Section 4.8, adds an Impact Statement, and moves software information into Appendix I. The overall narrative and most appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The water learning curve is redrawn with revised axes, legends, and initialization markers, appearing as v2 Figures 4 and 11 instead of v1 Figure 10. V2 adds OC20 Figure 12 and relocates Table 2. Other scientific plots are retained, with renumbering and limited layout changes.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the fine-tuning recommendation through the additional OC20 experiment, clearer accounting of pretraining cost, and more explicit presentation in Section 4.8 and Appendix G. Its specific archive access information also improves reproducibility documentation. These limited gains outweigh the loss of the nanoPET/metatrain reference; the paper's central evidence and conclusions remain largely unchanged.
